messages:
maria: FYI last night's nightly eval shows a sharp regression on the 'instr-follow' promptset for model 'falcon-2-large-int8' (~+11.8% failure rate). I attached the failing sample list.
kevin: ugh. Is it across all shards or just the quantized variants?
sophia: only the int8 variants (both quant-config-A and -B). float32 baselines look fine.
kevin: ok can you paste an example failure and the generation?
maria: example below:
```
PROMPT: "Translate:    Hello world\n"
EXPECTED: "Hola mundo"
PRED: "ERROR: context mismatch"
```
kevin: weird null bytes in the output.
dave: could be a KV cache / prefix reuse bug. ops-bot: deploy-logs for last deploy: runtime/v1.42 -> kernel dedupe cache enabled.
sophia: timeline: we rolled kernel dedupe last night at 02:10 UTC, nightly run at 03:00. Also sentencepiece was bumped in model onboarding script a few days ago but that didn't touch hosted models until a packaging job last night.
maria: hypothesis: dedupe cache uses token-id fingerprint but tokenizer change altered ids for leading whitespace/indentation, so two different textual prefixes ended up mapping to the same fingerprint or vice-versa, causing stale KV reuse.
kevin: can we reproduce locally? try tokenizing the failing prompt with old vs new tokenizer.
sophia: ran a quick repro: with sentencepiece v0.1.96 vs v0.1.97
```
old_ids: [1, 345, 78]
new_ids: [101, 345, 78]
fingerprint_old = hash([1,345,78], model_cfg) -> 0xabc
fingerprint_new = hash([101,345,78], model_cfg) -> 0xabc  # bug: hashing only used suffix window
```
kevin: ah so the fingerprint function only looked at a suffix window and ignored the initial token id, so different tokenizations collapsed to same key.
sophia: that leads to wrong KV being used for prompt A while serving prompt B -> attention state mismatch -> garbage/tokens/out-of-vocab output.
dave: root cause summary: caching dedupe optimization + tokenizer token-id changes = cache collision. The tokenizer bump changed token ID for leading-space tokens; fingerprint logic didn't include tokenizer version nor full-prefix head.
maria: mitigation proposals:
- short: rollback dedupe cache in runtime immediately (hotfix)
- medium: patch fingerprint to include tokenizer library version + full prefix hash + model id
- long: add gating: nightly eval will now run a tokenization-equivalence test for new model onboardings and packaging jobs; fail packaging if tokenization mapping changes vs stored baseline
- canary: enable dedupe only for models that pass tokenization-equivalence and during canary window
kevin: action items:
- @ops-bot start rollback-deploy runtime/v1.42 -> runtime/v1.41 (dave)
- @sophia prepare fingerprint patch and unit tests (include tokenizer.version in key) (sophia)
- @maria add tokenization-equivalence check to eval pipeline + add test vectors (maria)
- kev: I'll own canary gating config in rollout system (kevin)
dave: I've kicked the rollback, build id 2026-03-20-ops-rollback in progress :rocket:
ops-bot: rollback job queued, ETA ~4m.
sophia: I've got a WIP PR for the fingerprint change, adding tokenizer.version and full prefix; will push tests.
maria: once rollback lands can we re-run nightly eval quickly? we should validate failure rate drops.
sophia: yes, will trigger a targeted eval run after deploy completes.
kevin: longer-term: add a pre-release model packaging check that computes and stores tokenizer fingerprint and rejects package if token id diffs exceed threshold. Also pin sentencepiece in packaging pipeline for reproducibility.
maria: note: this was subtle — glad the nightly eval caught it. please add notes to the model-onboarding runbook and include rollback + canary steps.
dave: logging/todo: add telemetry to cache-hit path to surface tokenizer.version used for each fingerprint (low overhead). will follow up.
maria: thanks all. I'll post a short root-cause writeup after we confirm the rollback fixes nightly.
kevin: :thumbsup:
